title: Notice — The Charge for a Payment Sent Back Unpaid on Belrose Promotional Financing Plans
content:
# Notice — The Charge for a Payment Sent Back Unpaid on Belrose Promotional Financing Plans

A payment on a Belrose Promotional Financing Plan that the bank has sent back unpaid carries a returned-payment charge, worked out as the base charge for the return less every allowance the desk grants against it, and charged against the returned payment entry itself.

**Which return is answered.** The returned payment the charge answers is the most recently presented payment the bank has sent back unpaid on the plan.

**The base charge.** The base charge is the term's returned payment fee, as the fee schedule states it for the plan's promotional term.

**The allowances.** The allowances the desk grants are the channel allowance, the coverage allowance and the standing allowance, and each of them is worked out on its own and taken off the base charge once, so that they are never applied one to the result of another. No channel allowance is granted. No coverage allowance is granted. No standing allowance is granted.

**The charge.** The base charge less the three allowances is rounded to the cent, and where the rounded figure falls below nothing the charge stands at nothing.

## Worked figure (hypothetical inputs)

A payment presented on a plan written on a promotional term whose returned payment fee is 32.00 USD comes back unpaid, and it is the most recently presented payment the bank has sent back on that plan. The base charge is 32.00 USD. The channel allowance is nothing, the coverage allowance is nothing and the standing allowance is nothing, so 32.00 USD less nothing, less nothing and less nothing is 32.00 USD; rounded to the cent the charge is **32.00 USD**, booked against that returned payment entry.

Because the three allowances are each worked out on the base charge and never on one another, a charge of 32.00 USD answered by allowances of 6.00 USD, 8.00 USD and 5.00 USD would stand at 32.00 USD less 19.00 USD, that is 13.00 USD, and never at a figure reached by taking one allowance off the result of another.
